_comment: signal_modulation/design01b_twotone — NONLINEARITY BY THE FREQUENCY METHOD (two-tone intermodulation), on the design01 Nd:YAG amplifier, unchanged geometry, unchanged pump (Ez 808 from above, amp 50) and unchanged SGMA 1.86e-5. WHAT IT MEASURES: a LINEAR medium returns only the frequencies it was given. A saturating amplifier mixes them: the beat between two co-located tones modulates the inversion, the inversion modulates the gain, and the gain re-modulates both tones — putting power at 2f1-f2 and 2f2-f1 (third order), then 3f1-2f2 etc. Their power relative to the fundamentals IS the nonlinearity, and which orders appear give its order. This is the frequency-domain counterpart of the amplitude transfer curve already measured (gain 1.35 -> 1.0 across drive 1 -> 250, 2026-09-01): the transfer curve says the medium compresses, this says it MIXES — which is the property a reservoir actually needs. Note a resonant gain medium has no chi(2)/chi(3): there is no second harmonic at 532 nm to look for, the whole signature lives in the intermodulation sidebands inside the gain line. TONE CHOICE (the design constraint): both tones must sit INSIDE the 159 GHz gain line (gammaE 5.3e-4 FWHM) or the second one is not amplified and nothing mixes. Tones are placed symmetrically at +-0.5 HWHM (Lorentzian gain 0.80 of peak each), separation df = 2.65e-4 = half the FWHM. The third-order sidebands then land at +-1.5 HWHM (gain 0.31) and the fifth at +-2.5 HWHM (0.14) — generated by the nonlinearity and still amplified on the way out. WHY THE RUN IS LONG (18000, not the 3000 the saturation sweep needs): a DFT resolves df only if the window T satisfies df*T >> 1. T = 16000 gives df*T = 4.2, i.e. the sidebands sit ~4 resolution elements off the fundamentals. Shorter and the tones and their sidebands are one smear. The narrow gain line is what forces this: it caps df, and the cap sets the run length. dft_t_start 2000 clears the relaxation-oscillation transient (settled by ~2000 at every drive; see design01). AMPLITUDE: 40 per tone, so the beat peak is 80 — the ceiling agreed 2026-09-01 (drive 100 drove the population solver to unphysical values, level 3 to -0.40 and level 1 to 1.40, during the first ring). RMS-equivalent single-tone drive is 57. READ OUT: monitor_4 / monitor_3 (fine 1Ddft, 0.025 nm bins) for the exit and input spectra, and — the better instrument — snap_point's time trace, FFT'd OFFLINE with a Hann window: a rectangular DFT's sidelobes are -13 dB and would bury a percent-level sideband one resolution element away, a Hann window's are -31 dB and fall as f^-3. Created 2026-09-01 from design01.

crystal._comment: the Nd:YAG block. sted = the same 4-level Maxwell-Bloch machinery as the dyes, with Nd:YAG's lines: lbdA 0.808, lbdE 1.064, REAL linewidths. SGMA x N is the scaled doping (see top comment).

sted._comment: 4-level Nd:YAG starting FULLY INVERTED (N3_0=30, N1_0=0): the 230 us upper-level lifetime means a pre-pumped crystal simply IS in this state when a ps-scale signal arrives. SGMA 1.86e-5 = x30 the literal 1 at.% Nd:YAG value (6.2e-7), giving gL ~= 2.3 over the 20 um block — visible gain without free-running. CORRECTED 2026-09-01: the first pilot shipped SGMA 2e-3, which is gL ~= 249; the crystal dumped 97% of its inversion within 1000 t.u. REGARDLESS of drive (identical at amp 1 and amp 100) and amp 100 went non-finite at t=2281. That is parasitic free-running, not modulation. Calibration used: alpha ~ 1.1*(SGMA*N) /um at gamma=0.1, with the Lorentzian PEAK scaling as 1/gamma — the 1/gamma factor is what makes a narrow crystal line so much more sensitive to SGMA than our broad dyes (190x here).

source_1._comment: tone 1: CW Ey at 1.064150 um = line centre - 0.5 HWHM. Amplitude 40; with tone 2 the beat peak is 80.

source_pump._comment: 808 nm CW pump entering the crystal FROM ABOVE: y-normal sheet on the crystal's top edge radiating down (SimpleSim free source placement, 2026-09-01). Ez, orthogonal to the Ey signal, so they never interfere directly; the crystal is isotropic so the pump still drives 1->4.

snap_point._comment: exit time trace, dt 0.2 (17 samples per optical period). THE primary instrument for this design: FFT it offline with a Hann window to get the intermodulation spectrum without the rectangular-DFT leakage that the 1Ddft monitors carry. Also shows the beat envelope directly — period 1/df = 3774 t.u. — and saturation flattens its peaks.

pop_monitor._comment: Level populations N_l(t) AVERAGED over the crystal — the modulator's own state variable, and the cleanest read of when emission balances refill (N3 flattens). NOTE: no snap_interval on purpose. With snap_interval > 0 this sensor also stores the whole-cell snap_N (n_snaps, n_levels, Nx, Ny) + snap_E, which at 6000 t.u. is GBs per task; without it save() writes only {t, N}, the summed per-level series (sensor.py:305).

source_2._comment: tone 2: CW Ey at 1.063850 um = line centre + 0.5 HWHM. SAME position, SAME size as tone 1 — the two sources sit on top of each other so the crystal sees one beating field, not two beams.

monitor_3._comment: fine input spectrum, 0.025 nm bins over +-5 HWHM of the gain line — the two driven tones, for reference.

monitor_4._comment: fine EXIT spectrum, same bins — where the intermodulation sidebands at 2f1-f2 (1.064450 um) and 2f2-f1 (1.063550 um) appear if the medium is nonlinear.
